transcript.text: Good morning everyone. We've got four steel coils — C1, C2, C3, and C4 — sitting at the receiving dock because the labels don't match the mill-certificate packet. Each coil is 300 kilograms, and they're intended for two active production jobs. Before I can make a binding disposition and release any material, I need each of your formal status facts on the record. So let's go through the routine: Quality Assurance, Materials Engineering, Production Control, and Environmental Health and Safety — please each give me your status on these coils so we can get this resolved today.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Quality Assurance status: My receiving inspection this morning found that the certificate mismatch requires 100% positive-material-identification testing on all four coils before any of them can be released. The inspection is complete, but the inspection worksheet is still waiting to be attached to the receiving record.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Materials Engineering status: My handheld PMI test this morning confirmed that C1 and C2 are grade 304 stainless steel, and C3 and C4 are grade 316 stainless steel. The results are still in my instrument's export queue, so the formal report isn't attached to the receiving record yet, but the identity check is complete.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Production Control status: My current production schedule assigns exactly 600 kilograms of grade 304 to Job Alpha for Thursday and exactly 600 kilograms of grade 316 to Job Beta for Monday. I issued the schedule revision this afternoon, but it has not yet been entered in the receiving disposition system.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Environmental Health and Safety status: My floor review found that processing the grade 316 coils requires the dedicated chromium-bearing-metal dust collector and a 1.5-meter exclusion boundary around the cutting station. I recorded the finding during today's walk-through, but the temporary-control notice has not yet been posted.
